preconditions.expression: all(0 <= x < len(A) for x in A)
preconditions.description: Every element in A is a valid index within the bounds of A (0 ≤ A[i] < N, where N = len(A)).
All elements in A are distinct (no duplicates).
The length of A (N) is within the range [1, 20000].

postconditions.expression: return_value == max(len(set(S)) for i in range(len(A)) for S in [set() if i in set(S) else set() for _ in range(len(A))] for x in [i] for set(S).add(x) for _ in range(len(A)) for y in [A[x]] for set(S).add(y) if y not in S else None for x in [y] for _ in range(len(A)) if x not in S else None))
postconditions.description: The returned value is the length of the longest set S, where S is constructed by starting at index i, repeatedly applying A[x] to the last element in S until a duplicate is encountered. The set S is defined as {A[i], A[A[i]], A[A[A[i]]], ..., A[...]} until a duplicate is found.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= return_value <= len(A) for _ in range(1))
postconditions.description: The returned value is a positive integer between 1 and the length of A (inclusive), representing the size of the longest valid set S.
